Project Overview

This is a fully funded PhD studentship in Dr Dominique Laniel's research group at the School of Physics and Astronomy, investigating the chemistry of lanthanide and actinide metals and oxides under extreme conditions.

Research Focus

  • High-Pressure Chemistry: Behavior of lanthanide and actinide compounds under extreme pressures
  • Synthesis of Novel Materials: Creating new compounds with unique properties
  • Crystallography: Determining structures of high-pressure phases
  • Electronic Properties: Investigating electronic behavior under compression
  • Nuclear Materials: Understanding materials relevant to nuclear energy

Funding & Benefits

  • Tuition Fees: Full coverage (UK/EU rate) for 3.5-4 years
  • Stipend: £21,805 (2026/27 UKRI minimum) per year (UKRI rate) for 3.5-4 years
  • Research Costs: Access to high-pressure facilities and synchrotron sources
  • Travel: Funding for international conferences and experiments

Eligibility Criteria

  • Strong undergraduate degree in Physics, Chemistry, Materials Science, or related field
  • Interest in extreme conditions research
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities
  • Willingness to work at international facilities
  • Residency: UK/EU students

Application Process

  1. Contact supervisor
  2. Discuss research interests
  3. Submit application through university system
  4. Provide academic documents
  5. Interview process
  6. Award notification

  • UK/EU students.
  • Unique research on materials under conditions not found on Earth.
  • Access to synchrotron sources and high-pressure labs.
  • Research applicable to nuclear energy and waste management.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: Open all year - Rolling basis. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
